page: Amazon Web Services r6g.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by AWS Graviton2 processors built on the arm64 ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.5 GHz with a single execution thread per core, eliminating hyper-threading contention. It includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache, backed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture.

Hardware provisioning delivers 32 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio suited for data-dense workloads. The configuration includes no local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs present on the system.

Benchmark results demonstrate balanced memory throughput alongside modest compute capabilities. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 70.15 GB/s, while write performance achieved 34.19 GB/s, placing both in the median tier. PassMark database operations scored 2,654.31, also ranking within average ranges. Conversely, compute-heavy benchmarks registered lower percentiles, with a multi-core Geekbench score of 3,156, a multi-core stress-ng result of 6,051.15, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 7.34 GB/s. Redis SET operations measured 4.73 million operations per second.

The 8 GB per vCPU ratio makes the r6g.xlarge cost-efficient for memory-constrained architectures that do not require intensive floating-point or vector operations. Because the Graviton2 core exhibits lower raw compute throughput than high-clocked x86 counterparts, it trades high per-thread performance for balanced memory density. It fits in-memory caches, distributed key-value stores, relational databases, and enterprise data processing services compiled for arm64.
description: Amazon Web Services r6g.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated physical cores built on the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-N1 architecture running at 2.5 GHz. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance pairs 32 GB of RAM with 4 vCPUs to establish an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, complemented by 32 MB of shared L3 cache and a 1 Gbps baseline network link. The platform omits local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, depending on network storage for persistence. Benchmarking shows steady memory bandwidth with uncached large-block reads of 70.15 GB/s and writes of 34.19 GB/s, alongside average database operations performance. Raw compute metrics reflect lower percentiles across multi-core PassMark, Geekbench, and compression tests. This profile offers strong memory capacity per compute unit, serving in-memory caching layers, relational database engines, and medium-scale data analytics pipelines.
